paper_sections.title: Aging of visual word perception is related to decreased segregation within and beyond the word network in the brain
Data preprocessing for resting-state fMRI data

Between-group difference in resting-state functional connectivity

description.value: The study examined age-related differences in visual word perception using behavioral visual matching, a word localizer task, resting-state functional connectivity, and correlations between connectivity and word-matching performance.

design.value: The study recruited healthy older adults and young adults, collected resting-state and task fMRI data, identified word-selective ventral occipitotemporal regions with a block-designed word localizer, and subsequently assessed visual word and symbol-form matching behavior.

description.value: This standardized assessment is extensively utilized for evaluating non-verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) and indicates general cognitive ability.

task_description.value: This study first collected resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) data from all participants in a quiet state.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to keep their heads as still as possible during the scan.

task_description.value: After acquiring the rs-fMRI data, participants performed a localizer task that involved a simple location judgment task. The task included 16 blocks of visual stimulation and 16 blocks of fixation in a balanced order.

instructions.value: Participants judged the location of the stimulus by pressing the corresponding button as accurately and quickly as possible.

stimuli.value: Visual stimuli were divided into two types: Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters. Each picture was presented for 250 ms, followed by a 750-ms inter-stimulus interval. Stimuli were presented on either the left or right side of the fixation point.

task_performance_measures.value: location judgment accuracy and response speed

task_description.value: After completing all MRI scans, participants performed two visual matching tasks—word matching and symbol-form matching—in another room. The test consisted of 60 trials, with randomized stimuli and same/different trials.

instructions.value: Participants must quickly determine whether the two words on the screen are identical and press the corresponding button as swiftly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: The visual matching task included 30 new pictures of words and 30 new pictures of symbols, all in stick figure style. A fixed fixation point '+' was presented at the center of the screen for 800 ms. Then, two words appeared for 200 ms, after which a gray blank screen was displayed.

instrument.value: GE 3-Tesla MRI scanner (MR-750, GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain rs-fMRI data. The acquisition used 43 axial slices, a flip angle of 90°, a field of view of 220 × 220 mm², and a matrix size of 64 × 64. The resting session comprised 240 contiguous volumes.

instrument.value: GE 3-Tesla MRI scanner (MR-750, GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain task-fMRI data. The acquisition used 43 axial slices, a flip angle of 90°, a field of view of 220 × 220 mm², and a matrix size of 64 × 64. The task localizer session lasted 8 min and 10 s, resulting in a continuous time course of 245 time points.
Task-fMRI data were preprocessed using the DPABI toolkit based on MATLAB.

software.value: Data Processing and Analysis for Brain Imaging (DPABI) toolkit

steps.value: removal of the first five time points
spatial normalization to the EPI template in Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space
spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 6 mm

model_settings.value: The phase-scattered Chinese characters were used as a baseline; the linear contrast image was Chinese characters versus scattered Chinese characters.
The one-sample t-test was performed to obtain the group-level activation map.

For each participant, the Pearson correlation coefficient was calculated between the averaged time courses of the left and right vOT ROIs. Correlation coefficients were transformed into z-values via Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.

estimator.value: Pearson correlation coefficient followed by Fisher’s r-to-z transformation

model_settings.value: For each participant, Pearson correlation coefficients were computed between the averaged time course of each ROI and the time course of every voxel in the brain, then transformed to z-values using Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.

estimator.value: Pearson correlation coefficient followed by Fisher’s r-to-z transformation

model_settings.value: Between-subject variable: age group; within-subject variable: stimulus type.
Comparison of the connectivity values of the two vOT ROIs between older and young adult groups; the resultant t-value was thresholded with p < 0.05.

Two-sample t-tests were performed within the AAL mask, with gender included as a covariate. Gaussian Random Field theory was applied for multiple comparison correction, with p < 0.001 for voxel-level and p < 0.05 for cluster-level significance, two-tailed.
Comparison of the difference in IES between word and symbol processing.
The mean connectivity value of each cluster showing significant between-group differences was correlated with the IES from the word-matching task; analyses used p < 0.05.

Partial correlations between the connectivity value in each cluster and the IES from the word-matching task, controlling for the IES from the symbol-form matching task; calculated using the ppcor R package.
